newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Abacan sees full NGO output in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Abacan sees full NGO output in Jan.

text.p: Canada's Abacan Resource Corp expects production from its NGO oil field in Nigeria's Niger Delta to hit full production of about 50,000 barrels per day in January, company chief executive Wade Cherwayko said on Tuesday.
Cherwayko said in a phone interview that the field, which started pumping two weeks ago after a series of delays, was producing from two of the development's five wells.
"We should have all the wells done and completed by mid-January," he said.
The field's output had been delayed because Abacan had decided to install gas compression units on the production platform.

Cherwayko said the company and its Nigerian partner, Amni International Petroleum Development Co Ltd, planned to start a development drilling program on the eastern part of the NGO field in 1997, install a second platform and bring the new wells on stream in the first quarter of 1998.
"We don't know yet really, until we drill the wells, what type of flow rates we'll have," he said. "We'll find out once we start drilling some development wells."
Abacan has an agreement in place with Total SA's marketing arm under which Total buys all the oil and condensate produced from the NGO field. ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
